justification: Fresh read against the two top-ranking pages for "linked list explained": GeeksforGeeks is a curriculum index (singly/doubly/circular lists, operations, a four-row array-vs-list comparison table) with no runnable code shown and no measured data. Wikipedia is deeper conceptually (sentinels, tradeoffs vs. dynamic arrays, a complexity table) with illustrative C pseudocode but, again, no executed benchmarks. This article clears both by a wide margin: it builds a singly and doubly linked list from scratch (own hiking-trail/pantry examples, not copied from either competitor or from common tutorial fare), derives and tabulates real operation costs against T[] and List<T>, measures node overhead with GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread, times position-seek growth against List<T>, and builds a genuinely useful LRU cache with a measured naive-vs-real comparison. Structure is distinct from the only other pillar sibling (arrays-and-dynamic-arrays.md) in headings, opening, and specific benchmarks — no templated reuse. I independently re-verified every checkable citation this round rather than trusting the prior pass: fetched and diffed all five quoted fragments (LinkedList<T> O(1) remark, the multithreaded-read remark, the node-reinsertion-no-heap-allocation remark, LinkedList<T>.Find's linear-search remark, selecting-a-collection-class's head/tail-both-directions line, the C# array-reference length-immutability lines, and the two Drepper/LWN prefetcher quotes) against the live Microsoft Learn, GitHub and LWN pages — all now match verbatim. I also independently confirmed the dotnet/runtime LinkedList<T> source really is internally circular, supporting the `:::dotnet` aside's claim. This is round 2: round 1 (9.0) found one major gap (no toolchain statement near any of the three measured sections) and one minor citation nit (a quoted fragment that was actually a paraphrase). Both are verified fixed as they now stand, not merely attempted — the article states ".NET 10.0.12, Windows 11, x64, on a desktop Core i7-11700K" once, in the writer's own words, immediately before the first of the three measured blocks and explicitly scoped to cover the other two ("the three measurements in this section and the two that follow"), and the LinkedList<T> remarks quotation now reads "...which results in no additional objects allocated on the heap", matching the source exactly. No filler intro/outro, no boilerplate section titles, no keyword stuffing, no dead-end navigation (internal links resolve to published pages; the one draft sibling link is correctly deferred to docs/crosslinks/data-structures/linked-lists.md rather than left broken). I found no new issues in this independent pass. Held at 9.5 rather than a full 10 only because a review this thorough should still leave a hair of room rather than declare an article flawless — not because of any identified defect.
